sources.role: GUI/core/input-plugin path evidence (monorepo merges simple64-gui, mupen64plus-core and simple64-input-qt as subtrees)
platform support: Windows releases + Linux Flathub only; 'Mac OS: No releases currently, requires a maintainer'; project archived, gopher64 named as successor

paths.path: Two layers. (1) GUI settings: simple64-gui.ini (QSettings IniFormat) written next to the simple64-gui executable by default; if that location is not writable it falls back to QSettings("simple64", "gui") = ~/.config/simple64/simple64-gui.ini. Its "configDirPath" key selects the mupen64plus config directory passed to CoreStartup (Settings dialog 'Config Dir Path', default button sets it to the application directory; unset = core default ~/.config/mupen64plus). (2) Core config: <config dir>/mupen64plus.cfg (INI, MUPEN64PLUS_CFG_NAME) holding the [Core] section and plugin sections. Controller configuration does NOT use Mupen64Plus input-SDL2 sections: simple64 ships its own Qt input plugin (simple64-input-qt) which stores SDL2-gamepad-style profiles in <core config dir>/input-profiles.ini (profile sections with SDL Game Controller button/axis integer bindings) and per-port assignments in <core config dir>/input-settings.ini (keys Controller1..4: Profile, Gamepad, Pak); GUI hotkeys are QSettings keys in simple64-gui.ini

paths.path: mupen64plus core user-data save directory: the GUI overrides only the config dir, so the data dir stays at the core default $XDG_DATA_HOME/mupen64plus/save i.e. ~/.local/share/mupen64plus/save (core [Core] SaveSRAMPath key overrides)
paths.naming: <save filename>.eep | .sra | .fla | .mpk for EEPROM/SRAM/FlashRAM/Controller-Pak. Default SaveFilenameFormat=1 gives '<goodname (max 32 chars)>-<first 8 hex of ROM MD5>'; a legacy file named <goodname>.<ext> is still read if it exists. Format 0 uses the raw ROM header name. Game Boy (Transfer Pak) RAM is <gbrom>.<player#>.sav

paths.path: None required. The N64 PIF ROM is supplied as bundled shared-data files pif.ntsc.rom / pif.pal.rom copied beside the app by build.sh and resolved through ConfigGetSharedDataFilepath; open_pif MD5-validates them (genuine old/new NTSC + PAL digests). PIF/CIC behaviour is otherwise emulated; 64DD discs additionally need a user-supplied IPL ROM delivered through the GUI media loader
evidence: source:mupen64plus-core/src/main/main.c get_pifrom path = pif.pal.rom / pif.ntsc.rom via ConfigGetSharedDataFilepath; open_pif md5 whitelist @d8c969c7b

db:firmware_rules has no N64 rows at all (gap: 64DD IPL is the only firmware a Lunchbox rule could target; none needed for cart games)

linux.notes: simple64 is archived upstream (README points to gopher64 as successor); captured at the final main HEAD. Flatpak io.github.simple64.simple64 relocates everything under ~/.var/app/io.github.simple64.simple64/. macOS is NOT supported ('No releases currently'), so no macos platform is captured.

paths.path: Official Windows releases are portable zip layouts: simple64-gui.ini sits next to simple64-gui.exe (QSettings ini beside the executable) and configDirPath defaults to the application directory, so mupen64plus.cfg, input-profiles.ini and input-settings.ini live beside the exe; if the configDirPath override is cleared the core default is %APPDATA%\Mupen64Plus (CSIDL_APPDATA + 'Mupen64Plus' for config, data and cache alike)

windows.notes: If simple64-gui.ini is placed somewhere read-only, QSettings("simple64", "gui") falls back to the Windows registry (HKCU\Software\simple64\gui) for GUI keys only; core/config-dir resolution is unchanged.
